species.call_description: Not treated as a sound-producing species in this network. Listed because it is the river's main sport fish, so a quiet hour is not a count of bass.
Hudson River spawning sturgeon. Low-frequency sounds have been reported, but this network does not score them as a routine call class, so a quiet hour is not a count of sturgeon.
Alewife and blueback herring on the spring run. Not treated as sound-producers here, so the activity index does not count them.
Rapid croaks that build into a chorus on summer evenings.
Low growls plus higher rasps from pectoral-spine stridulation. More common upriver.
Long tonal boatwhistle, often preceded by a short grunt. A lower-estuary night caller.
Dusk chorus of high pulses. One of the loudest warm-season sounds in this reach.
Pulsed swim-bladder drums, usually a short series of knocks.
